items.source_title: 1. Current Written Supervisory Procedures and AML Policies
items.description: Provide the firm’s current written supervisory procedures, AML policies and procedures, Customer Identification Program (CIP) procedures, customer due diligence (CDD) procedures, beneficial ownership procedures, OFAC/sanctions procedures, suspicious activity reporting procedures, and any related compliance manuals or supplements.
items.title: AML policies and procedures
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: Current; include versions used during audit period where requested

items.description: Provide a representation letter on firm letterhead, signed by the AML Compliance Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, and President or other appropriate senior officer. The letter should state that, to their knowledge, they are not aware of suspicious activity or activity that would indicate money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions evasion, fraud, or other collusive activity by any employee, associated person, client, vendor, intermediary, affiliate, or other person in connection with the firm’s business, except as previously disclosed to the auditor.
items.title: Signed firm representation letter
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured

items.source_title: 3. AML Training Program and Continuing Education Files
items.description: Provide the firm’s AML training program, training materials used during the audit period, training calendar, attendance records, completion records, attestations, testing results if used, and records of follow-up for incomplete or late training.
items.title: AML training records
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured

items.description: Provide a list of all clearing-firm reports used as part of the firm’s AML program. For each report, identify its purpose, frequency, parameters, responsible reviewer, review and escalation procedures, and retention location. Provide samples for the audit period or, if more practical, the most recent three months.
items.title: Clearing-firm AML reports
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: Audit-period samples or most recent three months
items.condition_question: Does the firm use clearing-firm AML reports?

items.description: Provide a list of all other reports, manual checklists, screening reports, exception reports, or other materials used as part of the firm’s AML, CDD, CIP, sanctions, or suspicious-activity-review processes. Identify the purpose, frequency, preparer, reviewer, and escalation process for each item.
items.title: Other AML reports and checklists

items.description: Provide written information regarding the computer systems, vendor platforms, screening tools, manual controls, and other technology used for the firm’s AML program. Identify a knowledgeable person available to discuss such systems and controls, if applicable.

items.description: Provide samples of a new-client, new-engagement, account-opening, advisory, investment-banking, engagement, due-diligence, CIP, CDD, beneficial ownership, sanctions-screening, and risk-rating forms currently in use.

items.source_title: 8. List of New Accounts and Engagements
items.description: Provide a list of all accounts opened and all actual or prospective M&A, capital-raising, fairness-opinion, or other investment-banking engagements accepted, terminated, or completed during the audit period. Include client name, engagement type, date, industry, domestic or foreign status, transaction value or expected value, and disposition.
items.title: New accounts and engagements
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured

items.source_title: New Client and Customer Due Diligence Information
items.description: For the engagements or accounts selected by the auditor from the list provided under Item 10, provide the complete new-client/account-opening and due-diligence file. This should include CIP, CDD, legal-entity documentation, beneficial ownership and control-person information, identity-verification records, sanctions-screening results, risk rating, exception documentation, approvals, and any enhanced due diligence performed. (This will be requested AFTER this initial form is submitted)
items.title: Selected client due-diligence files
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured
review_notes: Source cross-reference to Item 10 requires Quinton confirmation.

items.description: Provide the general ledger for the audit period and, at a minimum, the most recent three months. Identify accounts used for advisory fees, retainers, success fees, referral fees, expense reimbursements, and other transaction-related receipts or disbursements.
items.title: General ledger
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: Audit period and at minimum most recent three months

items.source_title: 11. Foreign Accounts or Foreign Client Relationships
items.description: Provide a list of foreign accounts, foreign clients, non-U.S. legal entities, foreign beneficial owners, foreign counterparties, or other foreign relationships that engaged in business with the firm during the audit period. Include jurisdiction, engagement type, ownership information available to the firm, risk rating, and any enhanced due diligence or approval.
items.title: Foreign client relationships
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured
items.condition_question: Did the firm have foreign accounts, clients, owners, counterparties, or other foreign relationships during the audit period?

items.description: Provide reports or records of all customer and firm wire transfers, account transfers, journals, ACH activity, or other money-movement activity during the audit period, to the extent such activity is conducted by, through, or visible to the firm. If the firm does not handle, direct, or have visibility into such activity, provide a written representation describing the firm’s role and the extent of its access to such records.

items.description: Provide copies of all correspondence, requests, examinations, inquiries, subpoenas, deficiency letters, referrals, settlements, or other communications during the audit period with FINRA, the SEC, the Department of the Treasury, FinCEN, OFAC, the IRS, law enforcement, state securities regulators, or any other state or federal regulatory agency, to the extent related to AML, sanctions, customer due diligence, suspicious activity, fraud, or financial crime.

items.description: Provide a log of any Currency Transaction Reports, Suspicious Activity Reports, Suspicious Activity Report continuations, CMIRs, FBARs, Form 8300 filings, or similar reports made on behalf of the firm during the audit period and the prior two years, as applicable. Provide supporting documentation through a controlled process that preserves SAR confidentiality. Include documentation supporting decisions to file or not file a SAR, where maintained.
items.title: Financial-crime filings — contact auditor
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.

items.description: Provide evidence or books and records relating to any FinCEN requests, including Section 314(a) requests and responses, and evidence of applicable OFAC/sanctions and FinCEN-related screening or review procedures. Include related search logs, potential matches, research, dispositions, and escalation records.
items.title: FinCEN requests and screening
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured

items.description: Provide a description of, and access or demonstration as appropriate to, any system, vendor, process, or program used to screen new and existing clients, beneficial owners, control persons, associated persons, counterparties, and other relevant parties against the OFAC SDN List and other applicable sanctions lists. Include screening timing, list-update procedures, alert logs, potential-match review records, false-positive dispositions, and records of any blocked or rejected transactions.
items.title: Sanctions-screening system
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured

items.description: Provide the firm’s current AML/CFT and sanctions risk assessment and any prior version used during the audit period. Include the methodology, risk factors, risk ratings, approvals, updates, and documentation showing consideration of the firm’s M&A advisory activities, client types, transaction counterparties, transaction size, domestic and foreign exposure, ownership structures, fee arrangements, payment practices, intermediaries, products and services, and third-party/vendor dependencies.
items.title: AML and sanctions risk assessment
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: Current; include versions used during audit period where requested

items.description: Provide the most recent independent AML test report and all reports issued during the audit period. Include the audit scope, testing checklist or workpapers, tester qualifications, documentation of independence, findings, management responses, remediation plan, responsible parties, target dates, and evidence that corrective actions were completed and validated.
items.title: Independent testing and remediation
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: Most recent independent test and all tests issued during audit period

items.source_title: 22. Transaction Counterparty Due Diligence, If Applicable
items.description: If the firm conducts, obtains, or relies on due diligence regarding material transaction counterparties, buyers, sellers, investors, lenders, acquirers, affiliates, or intermediaries, provide the written procedures and records of such review for engagements during the audit period. Include sanctions screening, ownership information, enhanced diligence, escalation, and approval records, if any. If not applicable, provide a written representation describing the firm’s role and why such review is not performed.
items.title: Counterparty due diligence or representation
items.format_rule: Implementation defaults; source does not prescribe formats. Auditor review required.
items.review_period_rule: As specified in source request; engagement review dates must be configured
items.condition_question: Does the firm conduct, obtain, or rely on transaction-counterparty due diligence?
items.negative_answer_instruction: Provide a written representation describing the firm's role and why counterparty review is not performed.

items.description: Provide a schedule of advisory fees, retainers, success fees, referral fees, consulting fees, and expense reimbursements received or paid by the firm during the audit period. Identify any payment that was made by or to a person other than the contracting client or approved payee; involved a foreign or offshore account; was split among multiple parties; varied materially from the governing agreement; involved unusual payment instructions; or required an exception, escalation, or enhanced-diligence review. Provide supporting documentation for each identified exception.
